headline: Teenagers Around the World Turn the Tide on Plastic Pollution
meta_description: Over 3,000 teenagers across 25 countries are designing real solutions to plastic pollution through the Unplastify Challenge, avoiding an estimated 72 tons of p…
summary_short: Young people worldwide are tackling plastic pollution head-on, not just raising awareness—they're designing alternatives, changing school policies, and starting business…
body:
Since 2016, a global movement called the Unplastify Challenge has empowered teenagers to identify and solve plastic pollution in their own schools and communities. Over 3,000 students at 400 schools across 25 countries—from Singapore to Chile to Turkey—have participated in the program, which pairs young people with mentors to turn environmental problems into actionable solutions. The results are tangible: students have collectively devised over 1,000 strategies that have prevented an estimated 72 tons of plastic from entering the waste stream. What started in Singapore with students campaigning for reusable lunch boxes to replace 72,000 pieces of Styrofoam annually has blossomed into a diverse global movement.

The Unplastify Challenge, initiated by Latin American social enterprise Unplastify and funded by the National Geographic Society, stands apart because it treats teenagers not as activists raising awareness, but as designers solving a systemic problem. Students have created biodegradable glitter alternatives in Chile, replaced plastic sponges with natural luffa in Costa Rica, and worked with school uniform suppliers in Brazil to eliminate polyester fibers. The program teaches real-world skills—research, presentation, team organization, and project management—while students tackle issues they care about. Co-founder Augustina Besada emphasizes that the process itself engages young people: "They engage with other students, other schools, other countries, other cultures, other languages."

What makes this approach powerful is its refusal to settle for surface solutions. Rather than simply swapping plastic cups for paper ones, Besada pushes students to ask harder questions: How do you convince an entire school community to accept sustainable alternatives? That rigor has yielded results ranging from awareness campaigns and alternative materials to entrepreneurial ventures and policy changes. Five percent of participants have even engaged with regulation, working to install water refilling stations instead of single-use bottles. As global plastic production is projected to double in the next 15 years, these teenagers are proving that meaningful change starts with design thinking and community action.
quick_facts: 3,000+ students at 400 schools in 25 countries have participated
Singapore students prevented 72,000 Styrofoam pieces annually from schools
Over 1,000 strategies devised have avoided an estimated 72 tons of plastic
Students launched biodegradable glitter, luffa alternatives, and bulk oil businesses
Program launched by Unplastify in 2018, now running 12 annual challenges
